quote: This is not far from being a sign of our unhappy time, in which some who have attained positions as priests and teachers—merely to mention it is both distressing and sad enough—are consumed by the fire of heavenly vengeance because they prefer the fire of cupidity to the fire of heavenly love. Their eternal damnation was prefigured by the temporal death of Aaron's sons.

The sons of Aaron also, who set upon the altar a strange fire not commanded by the Lord, were at once blotted out in the sight of the avenging Lord. These examples, you will see, are being followed wherever the tradition which comes from God is despised by lovers of strange doctrine and replaced by teaching of merely human authority.
source_title: Treatise I. On the Unity of the Church 18-19

quote: Nor do we propose this, dearest brother, without the authority of divine Scripture, when we say that all things are arranged by divine direction by a certain law and by special ordinance, and that none can usurp to himself, in opposition to the bishops and priests, anything which is not of his own right and power. For Korah, Dathan, and Abiram endeavoured to usurp, in opposition to Moses and Aaron the priest, the power of sacrificing; and they did not do without punishment what they unlawfully dared. The sons of Aaron also, who placed strange fire upon the altar, were at once consumed in the sight of an angry Lord; which punishment remains to those who introduce strange water by a false baptism, that the divine vengeance may avenge and chastise when heretics do that in opposition to the Church, which the Church alone is allowed to do.

Let us see, then, what it is that has now been read to us. "And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying: You shall drink no wine nor strong drink, you and your sons with you, when you enter into the tabernacle of testimony, or when you approach the altar, and you shall not die. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, to distinguish between the midst of the holy and the profaned, and between the midst of the unclean and the midst of the clean, and to instruct the children of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand of Moses". A plain law is given both to the priests and to the chief of the priests, that "when they approach the altar, they abstain from wine and from every drink that can inebriate", which Holy Scripture is wont to name by the native word "sicera" (strong drink). The divine word wills, therefore, that the priests of the Lord be sober…

If, then, we have understood what the inebriation of the saints is, and how this is given to the saints in the promises for gladness, let us now see how our Savior does not drink wine, "until he drink it new" with the saints "in the kingdom" of God. My Savior even now mourns my sins. My Savior cannot be glad, so long as I remain in iniquity. Why can he not? Because he himself is "the advocate for our sins with the Father", as John, his fellow-initiate, declares, saying that "even if anyone has sinned, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the just; and he is himself the propitiation for our sins". How, then, can he who is "the advocate for" my "sins" drink the wine of gladness, whom I sadden by sinning? How can he who "approaches the altar" that he may make propitiation for me, a sinner, be in gladness, to whom the grief of my sins ever ascends? "With you", he says, "I will…

Priests given to wine are both condemned by the apostle and forbidden by the old law. Those who serve the altar, we are told, must drink neither wine nor shechar. Now every intoxicating drink is in Hebrew called shechar, whether it is made of corn or of the juice of apples, whether you distil from the honeycomb a rude kind of mead or make a liquor by squeezing dates or strain a thick syrup from a decoction of corn. Whatever intoxicates and disturbs the balance of the mind avoid as you would wine.

Scripture says, then: "the little breast of setting-apart and the arm of removal you shall eat in a holy place, you and your sons and your house with you; for it is given as a statute to you and a statute to your sons of the peace offerings of the children of Israel, the arm of removal and the little breast of setting-apart". Not every little breast is a "little breast of setting-apart", nor is every arm of "removal" or "separation" an "arm". But since we have recalled the person of the high priest to my Lord Jesus and to his sons the holy Apostles, let us see how he himself indeed eats the "little breast of setting-apart", and his sons, but the others cannot all eat the "little breast of setting-apart". What, then, is it that is set apart from all things and is not common with the rest, except the sole substance of the Trinity? If, then, I understand indeed the reckoning of the world,…
